title: Designer named once, on the invoice only
observation: The only place my name appears in the signed-in app is one line of brown text on the invoice: "Aspen Loft Refresh · from Leah Hartwell". Below it a heading reads "A NOTE FROM YOUR DESIGNER" with no designer attached. No photo, no studio, no credential, no contact — and nothing at all on Today, the project, the proposal, the decisions, the budget or the notifications screen.
why_it_matters: A client who cannot see their designer in the app stops treating the app as where the relationship lives and goes back to email, which is the exact cost the designer was promised this would remove.
proposal_seed: Mount a persistent studio identity line — portrait, studio name, one credential — at the top of Today for any tier with a project or an accepted lead.

title: Portal instruction for me rendered to my client
observation: The client's own project screen carries a boxed line reading "Set up phases, payments, and FF&E in the portal →" — an instruction written for the designer, displayed to the homeowner. It is a StaticText, not a button, so it looks tappable and is not.
why_it_matters: The client is reading the designer's back-office to-do list on their own project, which reads as sloppiness the designer will be blamed for and undermines trust in the money screens next to it.
proposal_seed: Replace the missing-section portal link with client-facing copy naming what is not ready yet, and never render a portal instruction on a client surface.

title: "CLIENT VIEW / Milestone" exposes the visibility tier
observation: A stat tile on the client's project screen is labelled "CLIENT VIEW" with the value "Milestone" — the raw client_visibility_tier the designer sets in the portal, shown to the client it governs, alongside "BUDGET $120,000" and "STATUS In Progress".
why_it_matters: Telling a client how much of their own project they are permitted to see invites the question the designer least wants asked and makes the app look like it is hiding things.
proposal_seed: Drop the CLIENT VIEW tile from the client app entirely — it is a designer-side control, not a client-facing fact.

title: Accepted proposal labelled "SIGNED"
observation: The list prints a section header "SIGNED (1)" and a card status "SIGNED" over "Sample accepted proposal / $100,000.00". The seeded account holds zero signed proposals; that row's status is accepted, not signed.
why_it_matters: A false signature claim on a six-figure design proposal is a legal artefact in the client's hands and is the single fastest way to lose a designer's willingness to send clients here.
proposal_seed: Split the accepted and signed states into distinct section labels and never render "SIGNED" without a signature record.

title: Sign sheet restates no amount and no terms
observation: "SIGN PROPOSAL / Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Type your full name to e-sign. Signing confirms the scope and kicks off your project." — then a "Full name" field, a disabled "Sign proposal" button and "Cancel". No amount, no line items, no date, no terms, no agreement checkbox — while the terms one screen back read "Deposits are non-refundable once procurement begins. Custom items are final sale."
why_it_matters: This is the instrument that binds the client to a non-refundable deposit, and it restates nothing they are agreeing to — which makes it worthless to the designer in any scope dispute.
proposal_seed: Restate total, date, and the two binding terms above the name field, with an explicit agreement checkbox.

title: Proposal expiry vanishes on the detail
observation: The proposals list card reads "Expires Sep 8"; the proposal detail it opens shows the title, "INVESTMENT $18,500.00", Design Vision, Concept Direction, Space Plan, Product Selections and Terms — and no date anywhere.
why_it_matters: The deadline is printed on the card the client leaves and dropped from the screen where they act, so the designer chases the signature by phone instead of the app doing it.
proposal_seed: Carry the due/expiry line onto the detail header, beside the amount.

title: Invoice due date vanishes on the detail
observation: The invoices list shows "Due Sep 1, 2026" on the INV-2026-0142 card. The invoice detail shows "Awaiting payment", "TOTAL $4,250.00 / PAID $0.00 / BALANCE $4,250.00", line items, a designer note and "No payments recorded yet." — with no due date at all.
why_it_matters: The screen that asks for $4,250 never says when it is due, so nothing on it creates the urgency that gets the designer paid on time.
proposal_seed: Put "Due Sep 1" directly under the balance on the invoice detail, and turn it red once past due.

title: Proposal selections carry no prices and no images
observation: Under "SELECTIONS": "Walnut sectional sofa", "Hand-knotted wool rug", "Walnut coffee table", "Reading lounge chair Qty 2", "Floor lamp Qty 2" — each illustrated with the Patina wordmark glyph as a placeholder and priced at nothing, against an "INVESTMENT $18,500.00" that is never broken down.
why_it_matters: A client asked to sign for $18,500 cannot see what they are buying, so the decision moves off the app and onto a phone call with the designer.
proposal_seed: Render each selection with its image and its line price, subtotalling to the stated investment.

title: No way to message the designer from anywhere
observation: The entire messaging surface is a Studio block reading "Conversation 0" and "No project conversations yet." There is no compose field, no thread list, no "message your designer" affordance anywhere in the signed-in app, on any screen.
why_it_matters: A client sitting on an overdue decision, an unpaid invoice and an expiring proposal has no in-app way to ask a single question, so every hesitation becomes a text to the designer's phone.
proposal_seed: Give the Conversation block a first-message composer that opens a thread when none exists.

title: Notifications empty while four items are due
observation: The bell reads "Nothing yet" / "Updates from your designer will land here." on the same device, the same minute, that the Studio lists "Decisions — 2 project choices are ready / Overdue · Aug 22", "Invoice — $4,250.00 remaining / Due Sep 1" and "Proposal — Aspen Loft — Living Room Refresh / Review by Sep 8".
why_it_matters: Nothing in this app tells a returning client what changed, so the designer's proposal and invoice are discovered only by chance and the designer does the reminding by hand.
proposal_seed: Write a notification_log row on proposal-sent, invoice-sent and decision-raised so the feed and the bell badge reflect the Studio queue.

title: Empty bell pitches a designer to an engaged client
observation: Under "Nothing yet" / "Updates from your designer will land here." the only control is a button reading "Get design help" — shown to a client with three projects, four proposals, an open invoice and a named designer on that invoice.
why_it_matters: The acquisition funnel is running inside an active engagement, inviting the designer's own client to request a different designer.
already_ruled: C4/U08 — the wording "Get design help" is canonical; its audience is not ruled
proposal_seed: Suppress the design-help CTA at activeProject and replace it with "Message Leah Hartwell".

title: Engaged home is the guest home verbatim
observation: For james.okafor@example.com — whose design request a designer accepted and claimed on Aug 18, and who has already uploaded a room scan — the home reads "Bring your first room into Patina" / "A short scan gives the Companion a real space to work from.", byte-for-byte the guest screen, with the footer "NEXT STEPS".
why_it_matters: The one true fact about this account — a designer took the job eight days ago — appears nowhere, so the client concludes nothing happened and the designer has to open the relationship by email anyway.
already_ruled: C23 — Option B's Today contract permits exactly one next move; which move is not ruled
proposal_seed: Make an accepted lead outrank the room ladder in the Next Move, naming the studio that claimed it.

title: Matched client's Studio is five zeroes
observation: The engaged account's Studio reads "Awaiting you 0 / Nothing needs a decision.", "In progress 0 / No active projects yet.", "Conversation 0 / No project conversations yet.", "Money & documents 0 / No shared records yet.", "Archive 0 / Nothing has been archived." — under a Profile reading "0 ROOMS / 0 SAVED / — MATCH" for a user with an accepted lead and an uploaded scan on the server.
why_it_matters: The pre-project window is exactly when a designer needs the client to feel something has started, and the app shows them a wall of nothing.
july_status: U22 delivered the empty-state copy; the missing fact — the accepted lead — is new
proposal_seed: Seed an "Awaiting you" row from the promoted design request so a matched client's Studio is never all zeroes.

title: Engaged client's only act is a second request
observation: "Your design request" opens on "No scans on this phone yet" / "You can scan a room to attach — or request design help without one below." with a single button: "Request without a scan". The already-accepted lead is not shown and there is no scan affordance on the sheet the copy points at.
why_it_matters: The title promises the status of the request the client already made and offers only the filing of a duplicate, which puts a second lead in the pool against a job a designer has already claimed.
proposal_seed: When a non-terminal lead exists, open this sheet on the request's status and stage instead of the compose step.

title: Money rail sits behind an unlabelled monogram
observation: The signed-in home is four elements — Next Move, editorial story, "ACTIVE ROOM / Living Room", Companion orb — and does not scroll further. Proposals, Invoices, Budget, Decisions and Projects live three acts away, behind a 36 pt unlabelled brown circle in the top-right corner, then a scroll, then the "STUDIO" block.
why_it_matters: Signing and paying are the two acts a designer needs a client to complete, and they are the two deepest acts in the app.
already_ruled: C1/C23 — no tab bar is ruled, and Option B's Today is accepted; the Studio's placement two acts behind the monogram is not itself ruled
proposal_seed: Mount the Studio's "Awaiting you" rows directly on Today whenever the count is above zero.

title: Three counts for one inbox, two on one screen
observation: One screen prints "4 things need your eye" as its subhead and "4 THINGS NEED YOUR EYE" in the footer, directly above a block headed "Awaiting you 3". Home and the Companion both say "2 project decisions waiting".
why_it_matters: Three different totals for one client inbox is a number the designer will be asked to explain and cannot.
proposal_seed: Derive every attention count on every surface from one BadgeCountService total.

title: "Your budget" shows $4,250 against $725,000 of work
observation: "BUDGET / Your budget / ACROSS YOUR PROJECTS" reads "$4,250 BILLED / $0 PAID / $4,250 OUTSTANDING", and lists only "Aspen Loft Refresh". The projects list for the same account totals $725,000 — Birch Hollow $185,000, Aspen Loft Refresh $120,000, Marrow & Vale Residence $420,000.
why_it_matters: A client reading "$4,250" under the word budget will believe that is their project budget, and the designer is the one who has to correct it.
proposal_seed: Rename the screen to what it computes — billed versus paid — and show project budget separately.

title: An $850 decision commits on one unconfirmed tap
observation: "Rug color - Natural vs Sand" offers two cards, each "$850" with an identical black "Choose this" button. There is no confirmation step, no way to ask a question, no defer, no "neither", and nothing states the choice is final.
why_it_matters: The shallowest act in the app spends the client's money and commits the designer's procurement, with no recovery path for a mis-tap.
proposal_seed: Route "Choose this" through the existing e-sign confirmation the code already contains, and add an "Ask about this" action.

title: A colour decision shows no colour
observation: The decision tagged "Color" — "Rug color - Natural vs Sand", "The jute rug from Studio Piet. Natural is warmer, Sand is more neutral." — presents two text-only option cards, "Natural" (badged "Recommended") and "Sand", with no swatch, no photograph and no rug anywhere on the screen.
why_it_matters: A client cannot pick a colour from prose, so the decision the designer raised to save a call generates one instead.
proposal_seed: Render the option image or swatch the portal already holds, at card width, above each option's label.

title: Overdue flag dropped on the decisions list
observation: The Studio row reads "Decisions / 2 project choices are ready / Overdue · Aug 22". The decisions list it opens — "DECISIONS / Awaiting your call" — shows two cards with no date, no "asked N days ago" and no overdue marker at all.
why_it_matters: The urgency is shown on the screen the client passes through and hidden on the screen where they act.
proposal_seed: Carry the due/overdue label onto each decision card in the list and onto the detail.

title: Piece detail is a hard trap with no way back
observation: Every product tap renders "Couldn't load product" / "Let's try that again" and nothing else — scan_ui returns exactly one element for the whole screen, the retry link. No Back, no nav, Companion greyed out and absent from the accessibility tree, edge-swipe-back dead. Reproduced in guest, signed-in, dark and XXL lanes.
why_it_matters: The one screen that would carry price, maker and materials to a client is unreachable, and the only escape is force-quitting the app.
already_ruled: C27 — named as genuinely app-side and fair game
proposal_seed: Qualify the ambiguous embed as vendors!products_vendor_id_fkey(...) and give the error state a Back control.

title: Sharing a piece hands out the designer portal
observation: Sharing a piece from the client app presents "Patina Designer Portal" / "app.patina.cloud" in the iOS share sheet.
why_it_matters: A homeowner showing a chair to their partner hands them a link to the designer's trade portal, under the trade portal's name — which is both confusing and a leak of the surface designers price against.
proposal_seed: Share a consumer-facing patina.cloud piece URL with an Open Graph title carrying the piece and maker name.

title: No commercial next step on any piece
observation: The terminus of every browse path is the primary button "Add to Room", which becomes "Saved ✓", plus back, "?", Share and heart. There is no Buy, no cart, no "Request a quote", no price-inquiry, no vendor link and no maker URL anywhere on any product surface.
why_it_matters: The app takes no money for goods, so a designer's client cannot buy anything here — which protects the designer today and means Patina earns nothing from the browsing it invests in.
already_ruled: C11 — direct orders are a ratified backlog item, not yet designed
proposal_seed: Offer a through-designer route from the piece — "Add to my project" for activeProject clients — before any direct-buy button ships.

title: A direct order would credit the designer nothing
observation: public.direct_orders carries id, client_id, product_id, product_name, quantity, unit_price_cents, amount_cents, currency, status, stripe ids, shipping, created_at, paid_at — and no designer_id, no project_id, no commission_rate and no FF&E link. The platform's own migration states it: "No designer attribution (client_id is the buyer)". The earnings ledger credits from invoice_payments only.
why_it_matters: The day a Buy now button ships on the client, a designer's specified piece can be bought at retail inside the app the designer sent the client to, with no margin, no schedule line and no notice — which ends the designer's willingness to refer clients.
already_ruled: C11/C24 — the rail is ratified backlog and the attribution decision is explicitly still open
proposal_seed: Add designer_id, project_id and a commission_rate snapshot to direct_orders before the client-side buy button exists, not after.

title: Browse grid is geometrically broken
observation: On "Browse pieces / 10 pieces curated for your space" the left column runs off the screen edge — "M & BOARD", "rloom Oak / ing Table", ",200" — while card frames measure 284×294, 171×341, 240×293 and 240×304 in a two-column grid, with one card ending at x=412.7 on a 402 pt screen. Reproduced in light, dark and XXL.
why_it_matters: This is the app's main commerce surface, and a designer cannot send a client with a real budget to a store whose prices are clipped off the edge.
proposal_seed: Pin the LazyVGrid to fixed-width columns with a uniform card aspect so every card is one size.

title: Product photography does not match the products
observation: "Live-Edge Coffee Table" by "LEE INDUSTRIES" is illustrated with an old ladder-back chair standing on grass; "Heirloom Oak Dining Table" by "M & BOARD" shows green velvet chairs around a white table; a card credited "UNKNOWN MAKER" shows a mint-green plastic pot.
why_it_matters: Provenance is the entire pitch, and a designer's professional credibility travels with whatever they send a client to look at.
proposal_seed: Hold a piece out of the feed until its image and maker are verified, rather than shipping a mismatched photo.

title: Studio rows unreachable by VoiceOver
observation: scan_ui on the Studio block returns none of Decisions, Invoice, Proposal, Active projects, Proposals, Invoices, Budget or Archive as accessibility buttons — only "Open Living Room", "Retake Style Quiz", "Get design help", "Settings" and Back. The rows draw chevrons and respond to taps. Reproduced in dark; at Dynamic Type XXL the same rows do expose a button role.
why_it_matters: The client's entire money and decision inbox is invisible to VoiceOver and Switch Control at default text size, so an assistive-tech client cannot sign or pay at all.
proposal_seed: Make every Studio queue row a real Button with an accessibility label and hint at all text sizes.

title: No sign out and no Account screen
observation: Settings shows "ACCOUNT / Account · Sign in on the web" — and the "Account >" row is inert, tapped dead-centre of its 338×44 frame with the screen unchanged, reproduced three times across guest and signed-in tiers. There is no Sign Out control anywhere in Profile or Settings; switching accounts in the walk required wiping the simulator keychain from the host.
why_it_matters: Two people share a phone or an iPad in most of a designer's jobs, and neither can hand the device to the other or leave the account.
proposal_seed: Wire the Account row to AccountView, which already contains the sign-out alert.

title: Project detail discards the data it fetched
observation: "PROJECT / Aspen Loft Refresh / Currently: Installation & Styling" renders three stats, an Invoices row and a portal link — while the network log shows the same screen successfully loading project_phases (3827 bytes), get_client_project_selections, project_payment_milestones and list_client_proposals. No timeline, no rooms, no phases, no selections, no install date, no designer.
why_it_matters: "Where is my job" is the question this screen exists to answer, and the answer was fetched and thrown away — so the client emails the designer for a status update instead.
proposal_seed: Render the phase timeline and the client-visible selections that are already loaded on this screen.

title: Completed project sorts above the live ones
observation: "PROJECTS / 3 projects" lists "Birch Hollow / Completed / TOTAL $185,000" first, above "Aspen Loft Refresh / In Progress" and "Marrow & Vale Residence / In Progress". Reproduced at Dynamic Type XXL.
why_it_matters: The finished job is the first thing a client sees when they go looking for the live one.
proposal_seed: Sort active before completed, then by most recent activity.

title: Guest's room and taste portrait adopted by the account
observation: After a guest session, client@patina.dev — an account with zero rooms and zero saved items server-side — shows "ACTIVE ROOM / Living Room" on Today, "1 ROOM" and "1 SAVED PIECE" in the Companion, and "✦ Modern Warmth / 1 ROOMS / 1 SAVED" on Profile. Your Spaces flags the same room "SAVED ON THIS PHONE" while every other surface counts it as account data. It cleared only when the local store was wiped.
why_it_matters: One household member's rooms and taste profile silently become another's, and a designer's client sees a home that is not theirs on the first screen after sign-in.
already_ruled: C27 — named as genuinely app-side and fair game
proposal_seed: Scope the SwiftData store to the signed-in user id and offer an explicit "claim your guest saves" step at sign-in.

title: No document surface for the client
observation: "Money & documents 3" contains only "Proposals / 2 shared proposals / 1 accepted", "Invoices / 1 shared invoice" and "Budget / Project totals and payment progress". There is no Documents row anywhere in the signed-in app, and project_documents filtered to client_visible returns an empty list for this account.
why_it_matters: Floor plans, spec sheets and elevations are what a designer hands over between meetings, and the section named for documents holds none.
proposal_seed: Add a Documents row to Money & documents that opens the existing DocumentListView, empty state included.

title: Push never fires for proposals, invoices or decisions
observation: apns-send is complete and provisioned, with exactly five callers: three design-request SQL triggers, fulfillment-notify (operator-initiated, on the BOH designer-sourced rail) and site-request-dispatch. Zero push callers touch invoices, proposals, decisions or direct_orders; notification-dispatch accepts channel "push" and writes a log row instead.
why_it_matters: A designer sending a proposal or raising an invoice has no way to reach the client's phone, so the app is not the channel and the designer keeps sending emails.
already_ruled: C14/C26 — C26 corrects the stub framing; the money-rail gap is the finding
proposal_seed: Add one invoke_edge_function('apns-send', …) call to the proposal-sent, invoice-sent and decision-raised triggers, on the pattern already proven three times.

title: Companion orb sits on the "Sign proposal" button
observation: On the scrolled proposal detail the fixed dark Companion circle overlaps and clips the primary "Sign proposal" button; at Dynamic Type XXL the same button clips the "Space Plan" body text. The orb also sits on "Browse Picks for This Room" in the room view.
why_it_matters: The single act a designer most needs a client to complete is physically obscured by a floating control.
already_ruled: C23 — Option B reserves the hearth as layout space; app content is not meant to render beneath the Companion
proposal_seed: Reserve the 120 pt hearth as bottom padding on every scroll view that owns a primary action.

title: "Your studio" row lands on a bare projects list
observation: The Companion row reads "Your studio" with the subtitle "PROJECTS · MESSAGES · DECISIONS" and opens directly on "PROJECTS / 3 projects" with a search field. Messages and Decisions are not reachable from that screen.
why_it_matters: The app's only navigation surface promises three destinations and delivers one, so a client hunting for a decision gives up two screens early.
proposal_seed: Point the "Your studio" row at StudioHubView, or rename it to what it opens.

title: Payment failure offers no retry and no human
observation: When the checkout hand-off failed, the screen printed one line of red body text — "Unable to start payment. Please try again." — inserted below a still fully enabled "Pay $4,250.00" button, shoving "Pay securely by card or bank transfer" half off the bottom edge. No spinner, no retry control, no support affordance.
why_it_matters: A client whose $4,250 payment will not start has no next step and no one to contact, and the designer finds out when the money does not arrive.
already_ruled: C27 — the underlying 503 is a local environment fault; only the failure UX is claimed here
proposal_seed: Render the payment error as PatinaErrorState above the button with a retry and a "Contact your designer" action.

title: An active project with nothing pending leaves Today
observation: The Next Move card reads "Review a project decision / 2 decisions need your eye." only while a count is above zero; the ladder is strictly ordered and, once decisions and unread messages hit zero, falls all the way back to "Return to {Room}". Proposals and invoices have no Next Move branch at all.
why_it_matters: Between the moments a designer needs an answer, a live six-figure project is invisible on the client's home screen, so the app stops being where the job lives.
already_ruled: C23 — Option B's Today is exactly one next move; the ladder's ordering is not itself ruled
proposal_seed: Give an active project a standing Today presence — phase and next milestone — under the Next Move card, independent of pending counts.

title: "Installation & Styling" truncated to the verb "Install"
observation: The project card shows "PHASE / Install" while the accessibility label carries the full "Installation & Styling"; the project detail one tap away reads "Currently: Installation & Styling". There is no ellipsis, so the phase reads as an instruction.
why_it_matters: The phase name is the designer's own vocabulary and the client's only progress signal, and it is rendered as a command.
proposal_seed: Let the phase label wrap to two lines instead of truncating without an ellipsis.
